title: Capstone Delivery, Demonstration and Evaluation
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Capstone Delivery, Demonstration and Evaluation.
Apply capstone delivery, demonstration and evaluation to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to capstone delivery, demonstration and evaluation.
Review common mistakes and risks in capstone delivery, demonstration and evaluation.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using capstone delivery, demonstration and evaluation principles.

understand.concept: A capstone demonstrates that a learner can combine requirements, design, implementation, testing, documentation and operational thinking into a coherent application. Evaluation should assess working behaviour, code quality, security, usability and the learner's ability to explain trade-offs. A demo is evidence, not a substitute for tests or documentation.
understand.whyItMatters: A structured capstone turns isolated skills into a complete and reviewable learning outcome.
understand.analogy: A final exhibition presents a finished artifact together with evidence of how it was made and checked.
understand.analogyLimit: A polished demonstration can hide defects; source review, tests and reproducible setup remain essential.
understand.summary: Capstone Delivery, Demonstration and Evaluation helps learners deliver and maintain reliable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Choose a bounded problem and write requirements before coding. Deliver in increments, keep a decision log, test critical workflows, document setup and limitations, review security and prepare a reproducible demonstration. Include known issues and future improvements honestly. Evaluate both the artifact and the reasoning behind it.
